title: Nutrient Allocation in Mycorrhizal-Plant-Herbivore Interactions
content: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) engage in complex interactions with plants and both aboveground (AG) and belowground (BG) herbivores, collectively shaping plant fitness, defense strategies, and AM fungal community assembly. A central question within these interactions concerns the role of nutrients. Growing evidence suggests that nutrients acquired by AMF not only enhance plant growth but also support both resistance- and tolerance-based defense strategies. Nutrient-derived primary and secondary metabolites exert systemically asymmetric effects on AG and BG herbivores through the plant’s metabolic network. These changes can trigger cascading responses in plants and herbivores, altering their performance in concert with abiotic and biotic factors such as plant and herbivore identity, feeding mode, arrival sequence, and damage intensity. Despite recent progress, significant gaps remain in understanding how AMF-mediated nutrients are distributed across ecological compartments and organisms within complex food webs. Moving forward, integrating nutrient flux analyses with mechanistic models will be crucial for predicting interaction outcomes under global change drivers such as elevated atmospheric CO₂ and nutrient enrichment.
